headline: Supreme Court calls police action against former Chief Justice Rana unacceptable
dek: Judges' Society and Nepal Bar objected, police blocked the rights commission at the gate, and the ruling party said nothing in Parliament.
body_markdown:
Nepal's Supreme Court held an emergency plenary session on Monday, September 28, and declared that police action against a citizen, even a former chief justice, without completing legal process is unacceptable in a democracy. Spokesperson and co-registrar Arjun Prasad Koirala said the judiciary must stay free of outside pressure and warned against acts that improperly influence pending or coming cases, Nepal Press reported.

That statement is the sharpest institutional rebuke yet in a case that has unsettled Nepal's legal establishment since early Sunday, September 27, when police took former Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher Rana from his home in Maharajgunj. Rana became chief justice in January 2019. He was suspended in February 2022 after lawmakers filed an impeachment motion against him. The Supreme Court dismissed that motion as moot on September 9, 2026, the Kathmandu Post reported.

It matters beyond one powerful man. The court's statement covered police action against any citizen, not only a former chief justice, Nepal Press reported. If the country's top court says a former chief justice was denied due legal process, the same question hangs over how police can treat any citizen picked up at night.

Officers reached Rana's residence around 12:30 am, and he initially refused to go with them, OnlineKhabar reported. Armed Police Force guards posted at the house first stopped the officers at the gate, the Kathmandu Post reported. Police spent about ninety minutes persuading him before taking him to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku. Police first called it an arrest. Hours later, Senior Superintendent Santosh Khadka gave a different account, saying Rana was brought in only because of a security threat. "After learning that there was a security threat to him, we brought him to our office at night because something could happen," Khadka told OnlineKhabar. No arrest warrant was produced, and no charge has been disclosed, the Kathmandu Post reported. Spotlight Nepal reported that police cited a complaint lodged with the Crime Investigation Office. Nepal Wire could not confirm that any complaint was registered. The Supreme Court's statement puts the detention at about 10 hours. OnlineKhabar's reporting puts it closer to 12. Rana was handed back to his family on Sunday afternoon.

The Judges' Society Nepal separately said Rana was not treated fairly even though state security personnel were already posted at his residence, Nagarik News reported. The Nepal Bar Association also objected to the police action and warned against arbitrary action, myRepublica reported.

## What the coverage missed

Two developments from the same day drew far less attention than the court's statement.

Police blocked a three member National Human Rights Commission team, led by commissioner Manoj Duwadi, from meeting Rana at Teku, keeping it waiting 45 minutes at the gate before it left without seeing him, OnlineKhabar reported. NHRC spokesperson Tikaram Pokharel called the conduct a violation of the commission's constitutional rights and demanded action against the officers involved. The commission has since summoned Khadka for questioning, the Kathmandu Post reported.

Rastriya Swatantra Party, the ruling party whose police carried out the detention, said nothing about it on the floor of Parliament on Monday. Neither did the main opposition, Nepali Congress, even though its spokesperson Devraj Chalise had already issued a written objection calling the government's explanations contradictory, Ratopati reported. Other opposition MPs, from CPN-UML and smaller opposition parties, did challenge the government in the House, calling the police action "state terror," Ratopati reported.

## What we still do not know

- What law, if any, was used to hold Rana, or whether a case was registered against him. Nepal Police headquarters or the Home Ministry could answer this.
- Why the security threat that justified taking Rana from his home at midnight had disappeared within hours, with no charge and no continued protection. Only Nepal Police can answer this.
- Why the National Human Rights Commission's team was denied access to Rana at Teku. Khadka, now summoned by the NHRC, could answer this.
- Why the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party has issued no formal position on a detention carried out by its own government's police. Only RSP's central leadership can answer this.

key_facts.fact: Nepal's Supreme Court held an emergency plenary session and said police action against a citizen without completing legal process is unacceptable in a democracy, spokesperson Arjun Prasad Koirala said.

Police reached former Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher Rana's Maharajgunj home around 12:30 am on Sunday, September 27, and took him to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office at Teku after he initially refused to go.
Rana was held for about 10 to 12 hours, with police first calling it an arrest and later saying he was taken in over a security threat, before he was released to his family on Sunday afternoon.

A National Human Rights Commission team was made to wait 45 minutes at the gate of the Teku office and was denied access to Rana; the commission has since summoned the officer in charge for questioning.
The Judges' Society Nepal said Rana was not treated fairly even though state security personnel were already posted at his residence.
Lawmakers from the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party and the main opposition Nepali Congress both stayed silent about the arrest during Monday's Parliament session.

social_hook: Taken from home at 12:30 am, held up to 12 hours, no warrant shown. Nepal's Supreme Court calls that unacceptable for any citizen, even a former Chief Justice.
take: Nepal's Supreme Court just told the government that taking citizens at midnight without completing legal process is not how a democracy works. Yet the loudest silence came from the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party, whose own police carried out the operation. The National Human Rights Commission was blocked at the gate. No one has named the law behind Rana's 10 to 12 hours in custody. Until police do, a midnight knock looks a little less safe for everyone.

EX CJ TAKEN AT MIDNIGHT
SUPREME COURT OBJECTS

caption.hook: Taken from home at 12:30 am, held up to 12 hours, no warrant shown. Nepal's Supreme Court calls that unacceptable for any citizen, even a former Chief Justice.
caption.body:
Police took former Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher Rana from his Maharajgunj home around 12:30 am on Sunday, September 27. He was held for about 10 to 12 hours at Teku's crime investigation office. No warrant was shown. No charge has been made public.

On Monday, Nepal's Supreme Court held an emergency full session and called the action unacceptable in a democracy. The Judges' Society and Nepal Bar Association objected too.

Police also blocked a National Human Rights Commission team from meeting Rana. The commission has since summoned the officer in charge.

The ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party, whose government runs the police, said nothing in Parliament about it on Monday, OnlineKhabar reported.
caption.trigger: If police knocked at 12:30 am and said it was for your own safety, would you go with them?

nepali.headline: राणामाथिको प्रहरी कारबाही अस्वीकार्य, सर्वोच्चको भनाइ
nepali.dek: न्यायाधीश समाज र नेपाल बारले प्रहरी कारबाहीको विरोध गरे, प्रहरीले मानव अधिकार आयोगलाई गेटमै रोक्यो, सत्तारूढ दल संसदमा मौन बस्यो।
nepali.take: सर्वोच्च अदालतले प्रस्ट भनिदिएको छ, कानुनी प्रक्रिया पूरा नगरी मध्यरातमा नागरिकलाई लैजाने काम प्रजातन्त्रमा चल्दैन। तर सबैभन्दा ठूलो मौन सत्तारूढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीकै देखियो, जसको प्रहरीले नै यो कारबाही गर्‍यो। मानव अधिकार आयोगलाई त प्रहरीले गेटमै रोक्यो। राणालाई १० देखि १२ घण्टासम्म राख्ने कुन कानुन प्रयोग भयो भनेर अहिलेसम्म कसैले भनेको छैन। प्रहरीले जवाफ नदिएसम्म मध्यरातमा ढोका ढकढकाउने आवाज हरेक नागरिकलाई अलि बढी डरलाग्दो लाग्छ।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । सर्वोच्च अदालतले सोमबार (२८ सेप्टेम्बर) आपत्कालीन पूर्ण बैठक बसेर कानुनी प्रक्रिया नपुर्‍याई कुनै पनि नागरिकमाथि गरिने प्रहरी कारबाही लोकतन्त्रमा अस्वीकार्य भएको जनाएको नेपाल प्रेसले लेखेको छ। पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीशमाथिको कारबाही पनि यसमा पर्ने अदालतले भनेको नेपाल प्रेसले जनाएको छ। नेपाल प्रेसका अनुसार सर्वोच्चका प्रवक्ता तथा सहरजिस्ट्रार अर्जुनप्रसाद कोइरालाले न्यायपालिका बाहिरी दबाबबाट मुक्त रहनुपर्ने बताएका छन्। विचाराधीन वा आउने मुद्दामा अनुचित प्रभाव पार्ने कामप्रति उनले सचेत गराएको नेपाल प्रेसले लेखेको छ।

अदालतको भनाइले पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश मात्र नभई जुनसुकै नागरिकविरुद्ध हुने प्रहरी कारबाहीलाई पनि समेटेको नेपाल प्रेसले जनाएको छ। यो कुरा एक शक्तिशाली व्यक्तिमा मात्र सीमित छैन। यो तपाईंजस्ता जोसुकै नागरिकसँग जोडिन्छ। देशकै सर्वोच्च अदालत एक पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीशले उचित कानुनी प्रक्रिया पाएनन् भन्छ भने रातमा उठाइने जोसुकै नागरिकलाई प्रहरीले कस्तो व्यवहार गर्ला भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठ्छ।

सर्वोच्चको यो भनाइ अहिलेसम्मकै सबैभन्दा कडा संस्थागत आपत्ति हो। आइतबार (२७ सेप्टेम्बर) बिहानैदेखि यो प्रकरणले नेपालको कानुनी क्षेत्र हल्लाइरहेको छ। त्यही बिहान प्रहरीले पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश चोलेन्द्रशमशेर राणालाई महाराजगन्जस्थित निवासबाट लगेको थियो। राणा जनवरी २०१९ मा प्रधानन्यायाधीश बनेका थिए। सांसदहरूले महाभियोग प्रस्ताव दर्ता गरेपछि उनी फेब्रुअरी २०२२ मा निलम्बनमा परेका थिए। सर्वोच्च अदालतले ९ सेप्टेम्बर २०२६ मा उक्त महाभियोग प्रस्तावलाई निष्प्रभावी भन्दै खारेज गरेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ।

प्रहरी अधिकारीहरू राति करिब १२:३० बजे राणाको निवासमा पुगेको र राणाले सुरुमा जान अस्वीकार गरेको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। निवासमा खटिएका सशस्त्र प्रहरी बलका गार्डहरूले पहिले गेटमै अधिकारीहरूलाई रोकेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। प्रहरीले करिब डेढ घण्टा मनाएपछि मात्र राणालाई टेकुस्थित काठमाडौं उपत्यका अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालय लगेको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। सुरुमा प्रहरीले यसलाई पक्राउ भनेको थियो। तर केही घण्टापछि वरिष्ठ प्रहरी उपरीक्षक सन्तोष खड्काले फरक कुरा गरे। सुरक्षा खतराका कारण मात्र राणालाई ल्याइएको उनको दाबी छ। "उहाँलाई सुरक्षा खतरा रहेको थाहा पाएपछि केही हुन सक्ने भएकाले हामीले राति नै कार्यालयमा ल्यायौं," खड्काले अनलाइनखबरसँग भने। प्रहरीले पक्राउ पुर्जी नदेखाएको र कुनै अभियोग सार्वजनिक नगरेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। प्रहरीले अपराध अनुसन्धान कार्यालयमा उजुरी परेको बताएको स्पटलाइट नेपालले जनाएको छ। त्यस्तो उजुरी दर्ता भएको हो वा होइन, नेपाल वायरले पुष्टि गर्न सकेको छैन। सर्वोच्चको भनाइअनुसार राणा करिब १० घण्टा हिरासतमा थिए। अनलाइनखबरका अनुसार यो अवधि झन्डै १२ घण्टा थियो। प्रहरीले आइतबार दिउँसो राणालाई परिवारको जिम्मा लगायो।

न्यायाधीश समाज नेपालले राणाको निवासमा पहिल्यैदेखि राज्यका सुरक्षाकर्मी खटिएका भए पनि उनीसँग निष्पक्ष व्यवहार नगरिएको बताएको नागरिक न्युजले जनाएको छ। नेपाल बार एसोसिएसनले पनि यस प्रहरी कारबाहीको विरोध गर्दै मनोमानी कारबाहीविरुद्ध सचेत गराएको माइरिपब्लिकाले लेखेको छ।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

त्यही दिन भएका दुई घटनाले अदालतको भनाइजस्तो ध्यान पाएनन्।

आयुक्त मनोज दुवाडीको नेतृत्वमा गएको राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार आयोगको तीन सदस्यीय टोलीलाई प्रहरीले टेकुमा राणासँग भेट्न नदिएको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। गेटमै ४५ मिनेट कुरेपछि टोली राणालाई नभेटी फर्किएको अनलाइनखबरले लेखेको छ। आयोगका प्रवक्ता टीकाराम पोखरेलले यसलाई आयोगको संवैधानिक अधिकारको उल्लंघन भनी सम्बन्धित प्रहरीविरुद्ध कारबाहीको माग गरेको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। आयोगले पछि खड्कालाई बयानका लागि बोलाइसकेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ।

सरकारको नेतृत्व गरिरहेको सत्तारूढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी सोमबार संसदमा यो कारबाहीबारे केही नबोलेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ। यो कारबाही यही पार्टीको सरकारमातहतको प्रहरीले गरेको थियो। प्रमुख प्रतिपक्ष नेपाली कांग्रेस पनि संसदमा मौन रहेको रातोपाटीले लेखेको छ। तर कांग्रेसका प्रवक्ता देवराज चालिसेले सरकारका स्पष्टीकरण बाझिएको भन्दै लिखित आपत्ति पहिल्यै जारी गरिसकेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ। नेकपा एमाले र साना प्रतिपक्षी दलका सांसदहरूले भने संसदमा सरकारलाई घेर्दै यो कारबाहीलाई "राज्य आतंक" भनेको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

- राणालाई राख्न कुनै कानुन प्रयोग भएको थियो भने कुन, वा उनीविरुद्ध कुनै मुद्दा दर्ता भएको थियो कि थिएन, अझै खुलेको छैन। नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालय वा गृह मन्त्रालयले यसको जवाफ दिन सक्छन्।

- मध्यरात राणालाई निवासबाट लैजाने आधार बनेको "सुरक्षा खतरा" केही घण्टामै किन हरायो, न त कुनै अभियोग लाग्यो न त निरन्तर सुरक्षा दिइयो, भन्ने प्रश्न अनुत्तरित छ। यसको जवाफ नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयले मात्र दिन सक्छ।

- प्रहरीले राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार आयोगको टोलीलाई टेकुमा राणासँग किन भेट्न दिएन, अझै खुलेको छैन। आयोगले बयानका लागि बोलाएका खड्काले यसको जवाफ दिन सक्छन्।

- सत्तारूढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीले यस कारबाहीमाथि औपचारिक अडान किन नराखेको हो, अझै खुलेको छैन। यसको जवाफ पार्टीको केन्द्रीय नेतृत्वले मात्र दिन सक्छ।

nepali.editor: Two sentences in the lede carry Nepal Press facts with no source, and the caption drops the 'about' hedge and places the pickup on Sunday night instead of early Sunday. Several sentences also read as translation and need the Nepali rewrites listed.

angles.claim: While opposition parties are described in the story as pressing the government, one major party, Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) — normally vocal on government process and style — has issued no formal position on Rana's arrest, with only a few leaders posting personal views on social media.
angles.why_it_matters: The story frames 'opposition leaders' as a unified bloc pressing government for an explanation; RSP's silence shows the political response is fractured, which matters for readers trying to gauge whether this becomes a genuine cross-party constitutional fight or stays a Congress-versus-government dispute.

evidence.fact: RSP leaders who usually question the government's decision-making process and style have stayed silent on Rana's arrest case; a few leaders shared views on social media but the party has issued no formal position.

angles.claim: An opinion piece published the same day as the Supreme Court's objection alleges a third procedural failure that neither the Supreme Court's statement nor the Judges' Society statement mentions: that police did not allow the National Human Rights Commission to meet Rana during his roughly 10-hour detention.
angles.why_it_matters: If NHRC monitors were denied access to a detainee, that is a separate, documented human-rights process question distinct from the judiciary's objection to the arrest itself, and it is being raised only in commentary, not in the official statements the mainstream coverage is built on.

evidence.fact: The piece lists three alleged police mistakes: arresting a former high constitutional office-holder 'under pressure,' citing a security threat as the stated reason, and not letting the National Human Rights Commission meet him.

angles.claim: Two independent Nepali outlets give a more specific chronology than the plenary-session story does: police went to Rana's residence at midnight on Asoj 10 while he was asleep, took him to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office at Teku, held him about 10 hours, then released him to his family — with no charge or case reported filed at that point.
angles.why_it_matters: The word 'detention' in the main story obscures that this had the shape of a formal criminal-investigation intake (a named crime investigation office, not a security holding facility) yet ended with no announced charge, which is the specific gap opposition and judges' bodies are pointing at.

evidence.fact: Police officers took the former chief justice from his home at midnight on Asoj 10 while he was sleeping, brought him to the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office in Teku, held him for about 10 hours, then handed him back to his family.
Confirms the same sequence: midnight arrest on Asoj 10, roughly 10 hours in custody before being released to family custody.

angles.claim: A same-day opinion piece frames the Rana arrest as 'just the latest example' of Nepal Police's moral-legitimacy problem, implying a recurring pattern of legally questionable police actions, but it does not name the earlier incidents it is comparing this to.
angles.why_it_matters: If there is a documented pattern of police acting on executive pressure rather than legal process, that is a bigger institutional story than one arrest; but as written the claim is an assertion without named precedents, so it needs to be checked against actual prior cases before it can be reported as fact.

evidence.fact: The piece states the Cholendra arrest is 'just the latest example' (पछिल्लो उदाहरणमात्रै) in which police's moral legitimacy has been questioned, without specifying which earlier cases it means.

investigation.summary: Beyond the Supreme Court's and Judges' Society's statements that every outlet is carrying, the Nepali-language record shows two under-reported threads: RSP's conspicuous refusal to take an official position while other opposition parties press the government, and an opinion piece's claim — absent from the official statements — that police blocked the National Human Rights Commission from meeting Rana during his roughly 10-hour hold at Teku's crime investigation office. None of the available sources, including today's story, identify any charge or legal basis for the detention, and a web search to independently verify or extend these threads was not available during this pass, so both should be checked directly with police, the Home Ministry and the NHRC before publication.

findings.passage: Judges' Society, Nepal Bar and rights body also objected, but the ruling party stayed silent in Parliament.
findings.problem: The dek promises that the Nepal Bar Association objected, but the body never mentions the Nepal Bar Association or describes what it said. The myRepublica source listed in the sources list for 'Nepal Bar Association's statement' is never actually used anywhere in the article text, so a reader cannot verify this claim from the piece itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence in the body reporting the Nepal Bar Association's specific statement, attributed to myRepublica, or drop 'Nepal Bar' from the dek if it will not be covered in the body.

findings.passage: when police took former Chief Justice Cholendra Shamsher Rana from his home in Maharajgunj.
findings.problem: The piece never explains why Rana, beyond his old title, is a figure whose detention matters right now. Public reporting shows he was suspended after a February 2022 impeachment motion and that the Supreme Court itself dismissed that motion as moot on September 9, 2026, just weeks before this detention. Omitting this fails the zero knowledge test the house style demands and leaves the 'why' of the story unanswered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one or two sentences of background: Rana served as chief justice from January 2019, was suspended after a February 2022 impeachment motion, and the Supreme Court dismissed that motion as moot on September 9, 2026.

findings.passage: That is a rare statement from judges who usually stay silent on live disputes.
findings.problem: No source cited anywhere in the article, or found in the wider record, states that the Supreme Court usually stays silent on live disputes or that this statement is rare. This is an unsupported adjective in the newsroom's lead opinion piece, which travels furthest of all the article's text.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the claim of rarity, or attribute it to a named legal commentator or scholar who has made that specific observation on the record.

findings.passage: No one has named the law behind Rana's ten hours in custody.
findings.problem: The body itself reports two different figures: the Supreme Court's statement puts the detention at about 10 hours, OnlineKhabar's reporting at about 12. The take silently picks one number, contradicting the uncertainty the body just established and misleading readers about what is actually settled.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the take to the body's own reporting: 'Rana's 10 to 12 hours in custody' rather than a single fixed figure.

findings.passage: Other opposition MPs, from CPN-UML, the Communist Party of Nepal and smaller parties, did challenge the government in the House, calling the arrest "state terror," Ratopati reported.
findings.problem: Nepal has several parties whose formal name includes 'Communist Party of Nepal', including CPN-UML itself, CPN (Maoist Centre) and CPN (Unified Socialist). Naming a second, separate entity simply as 'the Communist Party of Nepal' without a qualifier does not identify which party actually made the 'state terror' remark and fails the completeness standard.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Ratopati source for the exact party name (e.g. CPN Maoist Centre or CPN Unified Socialist) and use its full name on first mention.

findings.passage: Officers reached Rana's residence around 12:30 am, and he initially refused to go with them, OnlineKhabar reported.
findings.problem: A separate Kathmandu Post account of the same night describes Armed Police Force guards at the gate initially stopping the arriving officers, not Rana personally refusing to leave. This is a different sequence of events. Before publication, re-confirm exactly what the cited OnlineKhabar piece itself says, and if outlets disagree on this detail, report the disagreement per house style rather than presenting one version as settled.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-verify against the OnlineKhabar original text and, if the accounts differ, add a line noting the discrepancy between outlets.

findings.passage: No arrest warrant was produced, and no charge has been disclosed.
findings.problem: Same-day Nepali English-language reporting elsewhere states police said Rana was taken over a formal complaint already lodged with the Crime Investigation Office. The article's own unanswered questions section asks whether any case was registered, without noting that other outlets already reported a complaint existed. This is a real, checkable gap the piece could have closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask Nepal Police or the Home Ministry directly whether a complaint was registered against Rana, and either confirm and add that detail or note explicitly that other outlets' complaint claim could not be confirmed.

findings.passage: Judges' Society, Nepal Bar and rights body also objected, but the ruling party stayed silent in Parliament.
findings.problem: The dek groups the NHRC in with bodies that 'objected' to the arrest itself. The body's own reporting shows the NHRC's documented, on record complaint was specifically about being denied access to monitor Rana's detention, a narrower and distinct grievance from the Judges' Society's objection to the arrest itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase the dek to distinguish the two: 'Judges and Nepal Bar objected to the arrest, and rights monitors say they were blocked from checking on him.'

findings.passage: No arrest warrant was produced, and no charge has been disclosed.
findings.problem: This sentence states a negative fact about legal process in the newsroom's own voice with no inline attribution, even though house style calls for contested legal-process claims to be sourced to a named outlet in the same sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add attribution, e.g. 'No arrest warrant was produced and no charge has been disclosed, the Kathmandu Post reported.'

findings.problem: The house style requires the card headline to run two lines of five to six words each. This headline runs three words on line one and four on line two, thinner than the format calls for, which weakens its punch as a standalone screenshot.

red_team.summary: The story is timely, well attributed at the paragraph level, and follows the arrest closely with named outlets behind nearly every fact, but the dek promises a Nepal Bar Association objection the body never delivers and the article skips Rana's impeachment history that explains why this arrest is contentious. The lead opinion piece adds an unsupported claim that the Supreme Court's statement is rare and quietly resolves a 10 versus 12 hour discrepancy the body itself raised. None of the findings rise to defamation risk since allegations are consistently attributed, but several completeness and internal consistency gaps should be fixed before publication, and the card headline's line lengths do not match the house format.

responses.response: The red team is right. The Nepal Bar Association source sits in the sources list with a description of what it was used for, but no sentence in the body actually reports what the Bar said. That is a real accuracy gap: the dek makes a promise the body does not keep, and a reader cannot verify the claim from the article itself.
responses.proposed_edit: Add to the paragraph describing the Judges' Society: 'The Nepal Bar Association also objected, warning against arbitrary arrests of citizens without due process, myRepublica reported.' Keep the dek as written since it will now be supported.

responses.response: Fair catch. The piece assumes readers already know why Rana matters beyond the old title. House style's zero knowledge test requires the why to be answered without assumed background, and right now it is not.

The Supreme Court itself dismissed that motion as moot earlier this month, clearing the way for his possible return to public life before this detention.' responses.response: No source in the piece, or cited by the red team, establishes that the Supreme Court rarely comments on live disputes. That is the newsroom's own unsupported characterization sitting in the take, which is the most widely shared block of text. It should go.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the sentence to: 'That is a striking statement, since Nepal's Supreme Court almost never comments publicly on a case still unfolding.' If no named legal expert is on record saying this, cut the sentence entirely and move straight to the RSP silence point.

responses.response: The body carefully preserves the 10 versus 12 hour discrepancy between the Supreme Court's own statement and OnlineKhabar's reporting. The take then flattens that into a single number, which contradicts the more careful reporting two paragraphs earlier. Small fix, real inconsistency.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the take's line to: 'No one has named the law behind Rana's 10 to 12 hours in custody.'

responses.response: Nepal has three parties carrying some version of the Communist Party of Nepal name, and using the bare name without a qualifier does not tell the reader which one spoke. This is a real completeness failure the reader cannot resolve on their own.
responses.proposed_edit: Re-check the Ratopati story for the specific party name and replace the phrase with the full name, for example: 'from CPN-UML, CPN (Maoist Centre) and smaller parties' or whichever party is actually named in the source.

responses.response: House style requires reporting a disagreement between outlets rather than presenting one version as settled. If the Kathmandu Post account genuinely describes APF guards stopping police at the gate rather than Rana personally refusing, that is a materially different sequence and the article currently states only one version as fact.
responses.proposed_edit: Re-verify the OnlineKhabar original wording first. If it does say Rana refused, keep as is. If accounts diverge, add: 'Kathmandu Post reported that Armed Police Force guards at the gate initially stopped the arriving officers, a detail OnlineKhabar's account does not include.'

responses.response: The claim that a formal complaint had already been lodged comes from a single outlet, Spotlight Nepal, which is not in this article's sources list and was not part of the reporting the writer verified. House style does not require importing every claim from every outlet found afterward, only reporting faithfully from the sources actually used and flagging what remains unconfirmed, which the 'What we still do not know' section already does by asking directly whether a case was registered. Adding an unverified complaint claim from an uncited outlet risks stating something as established that the newsroom cannot back with its own sourcing.
responses.proposed_edit: No change to the published text is required. Before the next update to this story, a reporter should call Nepal Police or the Home Ministry to confirm or deny a registered complaint, and only then add a sourced line either way.

responses.response: This is accurate and worth fixing. The Judges' Society and Nepal Bar objected to the arrest and its manner, while the NHRC's documented grievance in the body is specifically about being denied access at the gate, a narrower complaint. Grouping them under one verb blurs a real distinction the body itself preserves.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the dek to: 'Judges and the Nepal Bar objected to the arrest, and rights monitors say they were blocked from checking on him, but the ruling party stayed silent in Parliament.'

responses.response: This is a contested legal-process claim stated in the newsroom's own voice without inline attribution, which house style specifically requires for this kind of fact. The source exists and is already in the sources list, so this is a one-line fix.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'No arrest warrant was produced, and no charge has been disclosed, the Kathmandu Post reported.'

responses.response: The card headline runs three words then four, short of the five to six word per line format house style sets for standalone screenshots. Worth tightening to spec without losing the plain declarative fact the record supports.
responses.proposed_edit: Change image_headline to: 'SUPREME COURT OBJECTS TO\nRANA'S MIDNIGHT ARREST' or, if that exceeds 24 characters on a line, 'COURT CALLS ARREST\nOF RANA UNACCEPTABLE', checking each line stays under 24 characters including spaces.

updates.text_ne: यो समाचारको शीर्षक, कार्ड र केही वाक्यमा राणालाई प्रहरीले लगेको घटनालाई पक्राउ भनिएको थियो। प्रहरीले सुरुमा पक्राउ भने पनि पछि सुरक्षा खतराका कारण ल्याएको बताएको थियो, र सर्वोच्च अदालतले कानुनी प्रक्रिया पूरा नगरी गरिने प्रहरी कारबाहीको कुरा गरेको थियो। अब प्रहरी कारबाही वा हिरासत लेखिएको छ। अंग्रेजी मूल समाचारमा नभएका चार अनुच्छेद र एउटा प्रश्न पनि नेपाली संस्करणबाट हटाइएका छन्।
